solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bachelor, say, crazy to put down fruit

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees like BA
to say something is to utter it
nuts is slang for crazy
to put down a revolt is to quash it

explanation.surface: A mad unmarried man is about to stamp on some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bachelor, say' looks like 'for example, a bachelor', but 'say' is its own piece, UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Butternut squash is a pale orange gourd, botanically the fruit of its vine.

clue.text: Youngster to yearn endlessly for ruined city

parts.note: a baby is the youngest of youngsters

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to yearn is to long

explanation.surface: A child pining for a city that lies in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon, the great Mesopotamian capital, survives only as ruins in modern Iraq.

clue.text: Bone idle at first during a little uprising

indicators.note: during puts the letter in the middle of the other pieces
in a down clue an uprising reads the pieces from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a bit is a little

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of idle

explanation.surface: A lazy person's bone, idle during a minor rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns A BIT into TIBA, and the I from 'idle' goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two lower-leg bones.

clue.text: Site of a battle in Basel — a lame insurrection

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: A feeble uprising in the Swiss city of Basel marks the place of a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein in Egypt saw the decisive 1942 Allied victory over Rommel's forces.

clue.text: River's inlet almost diverted

indicators.note: diverted means the remaining letters are sent off on a new course, rearranged
almost means the word stops short of its last letter

explanation.surface: A river's creek has nearly been rerouted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the T of 'inlet', and 'diverted' rearranges INLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is Africa's longest river; the 's stands for 'is', so 'River is' gives the answer.

clue.text: Plays conservative film

parts.note: to play idly with something is to toy with it, so plays gives toys
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Traditional theatre pieces become a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Toy Story is the 1995 Pixar animated feature, the first fully computer-generated film.

clue.text: Old writer briefly covers a game

indicators.note: covers means the shortened word wraps round the next piece
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a quill was the feather pen of the past

explanation.surface: A former author, in short, deals with a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' here means hunted birds, not a sport: QUIL goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Quail are small birds shot or reared as game for the table.

clue.text: Paintings by men put in suitable studio, maybe

indicators.note: put in means the joined pieces go inside the next one

parts.note: apt means suitable

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: Artworks by men hung in a fitting workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a one-room apartment, so a studio is one example of the answer.

clue.text: Most of repulsive regiment finally retreat

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: hideous means repulsive

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of regiment

explanation.surface: A largely disgusting regiment eventually falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reads as a military verb but is the noun: a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a secluded place to withdraw to, a retreat.

clue.text: Singer to surround source of beer, Spooner says

indicators.note: Spooner says means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: to mob someone is to surround them in a crowd
barley is malted to make beer

explanation.surface: A vocalist is told to encircle the grain that makes ale.
explanation.walkthrough: MOB BARLEY with initial letters swapped gives the reggae star.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley was the Jamaican reggae vocalist and songwriter.

clue.text: A fight ending in gold medal, perhaps

parts.note: a war is a fight on a large scale

indicators.note: ending in takes only the final letter of gold

explanation.surface: A battle ends with a gold medal won.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is one kind of prize given in recognition, an award.

clue.text: Area is overrun by flipping tiny creatures!

indicators.note: is overrun by means the first piece is swamped, enclosed by the second
flipping turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: tiny means small

explanation.surface: A district swarming with blasted little beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild curse but turns SMALL into LLAMS, which takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelid animals, kept as pack beasts.

clue.text: Toes tilt awkwardly in this?

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters are put together clumsily, rearranged

explanation.surface: Feet are tipped at an uncomfortable angle in this shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto heel forces the foot forward so the toes are tilted uncomfortably.

clue.text: Northern European that was close relative?

parts.note: phew is what one says after a near miss

explanation.surface: A northern European asks whether he was a near relation.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a sibling's son, a family relative.

clue.text: Beer batch served up in delicate containers

indicators.note: in a down clue served up reads the pieces upwards, backwards

parts.note: ale is beer
a crop is a batch of produce grown together

explanation.surface: A round of beers brought out in fragile glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns ALE CROP into PORCELA.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is fine china, used for fragile cups and vases.

clue.text: Survey the view

definitions.meaning: a wide view of a landscape

explanation.surface: Look over the scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospect means both exploring ground for gold and a sweeping outlook.

clue.text: Sand layer from ancient city covered by modern one?

indicators.note: covered by means the first city is enclosed inside the second

parts.note: Seattle is a modern city in Washington State
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A stratum of sand from an old city buried beneath a newer one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum; it is one that lays eggs, in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sea turtles crawl onto beaches to lay their eggs in the sand.

clue.text: Hot swimmer is accommodating at any time

indicators.note: is accommodating means the first piece houses the second

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
ever means at any time

explanation.surface: A sweaty swimmer is always welcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: A feverish person has a raised temperature, so feels hot.

clue.text: Document banks called crazy

indicators.note: banks means the first word lines both sides of the second

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Paperwork that banks phoned about is unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged means mentally unbalanced, insane.

clue.text: Part of pool table ultimately breaks bank

indicators.note: breaks means the letter splits the other word open

parts.note: to bank on something is to depend on it

indicators.note: ultimately takes only the final letter of table

explanation.surface: A snooker or pool table and a break that wins the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' suggests the cue game, but it is a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep end is the section of a swimming pool with the greatest depth.

clue.text: Plan start of play set in Titanic's hull?

indicators.note: set in means the first piece is placed inside the shell
the hull is the outer shell, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: Act I is the opening act of a play

explanation.surface: A scheme to begin a show inside the wreck of the famous liner.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre to gain an end.

clue.text: Merciful post-war prime minister, say?

definitions.meaning: ... Attlee was the British prime minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: A lenient leader of the country after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: Attlee led Britain's Labour government straight after the Second World War; 'say' marks his first name as just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather or a clement judge is mild and lenient.

clue.text: Naval agreement, we hear, with ship producing make-up

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken and replaced by another with the same sound

parts.note: aye aye is how sailors say yes
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A sailor's yes, along with an ocean liner, results in cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is a cosmetic drawn along the lids, a form of make-up.

clue.text: I help Northern Island from the south

definitions.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter I is called India

indicators.note: in a down clue reading from the south means from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: I assist a northern island coming from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the definition: the radio code word for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators say India to spell out the letter I.

clue.text: Not oddly worried after controversial coat causes uproar

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a fur coat is a matter of animal-welfare controversy

indicators.note: not oddly keeps the even-placed letters of worried

explanation.surface: Fretting over a disputed fur coat leads to an outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public anger, an uproar.

clue.text: Middle Eastern country without borders

indicators.note: without borders means the first and last letters are cut off

parts.note: Romania is a country in Eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A borderless state in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' looks like part of the definition but supplies ROMANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Omani describes something from Oman, on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Game's up for hawk

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: golf is a game; the 's stands for 'is' as a link

explanation.surface: Time to shoot a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' suggests the bird; it is the verb, to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk goods is to peddle them, and to flog is slang for to sell.

clue.text: Antelope I caught leaving the country

indicators.note: leaving means these letters depart from the country's name

parts.note: Iceland is a North Atlantic island country
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An antelope that I captured departs the land.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: A kid on medication, powerless and uncomfortable

indicators.note: on means the first pieces follow on from the medication
powerless means the letter P, short for power, is removed

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medication
to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A child taking medicine, weak and uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb, to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill at ease means feeling awkward and uncomfortable.

clue.text: Study hesitatingly prepared for oral examiner?

parts.note: a den is a private room or study

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made up into a new form

explanation.surface: Revising nervously for a spoken exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges HESITATINGLY into TALHYGIENIST. 'Oral examiner' sounds like a viva; it is someone who examines mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental hygienist checks and cleans teeth, examining the mouth.
